# Albena

> Albena is a private, local-first AI assistant for your home and life, made by Omar Huertas LLC. She runs on hardware you own (a Mac with Apple silicon, or an NVIDIA RTX Linux machine), uses local models first, connects to smart-home, media, work and cloud systems, and asks for your approval before she changes anything. Albena is in early access and is not yet generally available; no prices or launch date are published.

Facts, stated plainly:
- Voice-first: the wake phrase is "Hey Albena", processed on your own devices. Touch and keyboard also work.
- Local-first: everyday requests, audio, device data and memory are processed on hardware you own wherever possible. A cloud model is used only if a task needs it and you allow it.
- Approvals: reads are instant. Anything that changes something is proposed to you first. High-risk actions also need a change record and your PIN, with rollback information and an audit log.
- Memory: Albena remembers people, routines and preferences; the owner can view, correct and delete any of it.
- Connectors: Home Assistant, Philips Hue, WiZ, Google Nest, TVs, cameras, Jellyfin, Navidrome, Immich, YouTube, Google Workspace, Microsoft Teams, Slack, Jira, ServiceNow, GitHub, LinkedIn, Meta pages, AWS, Azure, Cloudflare, VMware, Docker, Kubernetes, Tailscale, AdGuard, Active Directory/LDAP and more, plus any REST API or MCP server.
- Editions: Albena Hub for Mac, Albena Hub for NVIDIA, Bring Your Own (software license for hardware you own), and Pro / Estate install. All are early access with pricing not yet announced.
- Security status: no certifications are claimed. Practices are aligned with frameworks such as SOC 2 and NIST 800-53 and mapped honestly in a public control mapping; independent audits have not been completed.
- Not yet available: native iPhone and Mac apps, published pricing, Albena Voice room satellites.
